hints.title: Cascading Run Cancellation Obstacle
hints.text: Repeated string scans and slice removals incur O(N^2 / k) runtime on cascading matches. How can maintaining an ordered record of consecutive character counts eliminate full groups of size k immediately upon arrival?

hints.title: Character-Count Pair Invariant
hints.text: By storing elements as [character, count] pairs, the top element tracks the length of the current uniform run. If count reaches k, popping the pair unmasks the preceding run.

hints.title: Count-Aware Reduction Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an empty list of [char, count] pairs. For each character ch: if the list is non-empty and its top pair has character ch, increment top's count; otherwise append [ch, 1]. If the top count reaches k, pop it. Finally, rebuild the string from the surviving pairs.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 10^5)
k: group size to delete (2 <= k <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Each character is pushed and popped at most once with count tracking.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Repeatedly searching for runs of k matching characters and slicing the string takes O(N^2 / k) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Pairing each character with its running count in an auxiliary list reduces total runtime to strictly linear O(N).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Storing run lengths alongside characters rather than storing k duplicate entries individually.
